merge_ruling.for_merge: H and V are one letter apart to a distance and one glyph apart to a worn impression, 'John' is identical, and both readings are the Democrat inside sixteen months.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THREE DIFFERENT ISSUES, AND NEITHER SPELLING EVER SHARES ONE. 'John Hale' is the Democrat of 16 April 1834 (#c005) and 'Hale, John' the return of 1 July 1835 (#c005); 'Vale, John' is the Democrat of 5 August 1835 (#c006). No issue sets both. Both stems are alive in the corpus — Hale 83 settings, Vale 33 — and neither card is an anchor: no trade, no street, no household on either. H against V is not the substitution a period compositor's case makes, and the reading index holds three Hale identities to Vale's one. D7.
